public_rationale: The disclosures establish relevant practices in individual model families. They do not establish that most contemporary models relied heavily on data generated by symbolic rules. Marcus's qualification acknowledges uncertainty, but the underlying prevalence claim remains testable. The available examples neither establish nor refute it.
limitations: The population and the meaning of heavy use remain unspecified.
The cited reports describe earlier training pipelines and serve as context for the post-date population.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Most modern models appear to rely heavily on training data generated by symbolic rule systems.

statement.excerpt: From what I can tell, most modern models also make heavy use of data augmentation that involves (inter alia) running systems of symbolic rules and training on their outputs, a far cry from the original notion of training on naturalistically-observed data and then inducing whatever needed to be learned.
statement.document_title: How o3 and Grok 4 Accidentally Vindicated Neurosymbolic AI

from_speaker: running systems of symbolic rules and training on their outputs
our_interpretation: Most means more than half of the relevant models, not merely several prominent examples.
Heavy use means a substantial contribution to training, rather than incidental filtering or preprocessing. Marcus supplies no numerical threshold.

The surrounding discussion concerns contemporary generative language and reasoning models. Model-generated text alone does not establish generation by symbolic rules; rule-based verification can establish involvement but does not by itself establish its extent.
The target is the model population current on the post date. There is no standard reporting period for this observation, so a point-in-time snapshot is used.
criteria.support_condition: Representative training disclosures establish that more than half of contemporary models substantially used augmented training data produced through symbolic rule execution.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative disclosures establish that half or fewer used such data substantially, or that the purported use was generally incidental.

evidence.locator: Section 2.3.3, Rejection Sampling and Supervised Fine-Tuning
evidence.explanation: The report describes rule-based rewards, compiler feedback, and approximately 600,000 selected reasoning examples. This establishes symbolic involvement in one training pipeline, but neither a majority of models nor the prevalence of training directly on symbolic-system outputs.

The surrounding sections describe increased synthetic-data use and generation by Qwen models. They do not quantify the share generated by symbolic rule systems; the entire five-trillion-token stage cannot be counted as such data.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A representative audit of models available by July 13, 2025, identifying symbolic-generated training data and its substantial contribution in each model.
